title: Heralded one-, two- and three-photon states from waveguided parametric down-conversion
abstract: The manifold coincidences and singles counting provides a resource-saving quantum-optics analysis tool, since it is appropriate even in the presence of heavy experimental imperfections. Here, we prepare cross-polarized twin beams in the telecommunication wavelength range via parametric down-conversion in a periodically-poled KTiOPO$_4$ waveguide and herald photon-number states up to three photons. First, we show that the single-click probability is a versatile tool not only for extracting the state's mean photon number but also for sampling values of the moment generating function being the core behind any quantum optical state. Second, we measure values of the normalized factorial moments of photon number, $g^{(m)}_{\text{h}}$, up to the order $m = n+1$ for the heralded $n$-photon state. These normalized photon correlations provide an expedient method for examining the higher-order non-classicality of light by violating the condition $g^{(m+1)}_{\text{h}} \ge g^{(m)}_{\text{h}} \ge 1$.
summary: The authors report on the generation and characterization of heralded multi-photon states using parametric down-conversion in a waveguide. They introduce and validate a resource-saving analysis method based on single-click probabilities and normalized factorial moments. The key finding is the quantitative demonstration of higher-order non-classicality by violating established classical light criteria.
main_problem: The paper aims to prepare and characterize heralded one-, two-, and three-photon number states using parametric down-conversion while demonstrating resource-saving quantum-optics analysis tools.
main_result: The measurements successfully characterized higher-order non-classicality by violating the classical condition $g^{(m+1)}_h \geq g^{(m)}_h \geq 1$, confirming the non-classical nature of the generated multi-photon states.
method: The analysis utilizes manifold coincidences and singles counting, which is robust against experimental imperfections, to measure normalized factorial moments of photon number ($g^{(m)}_h$).
model_or_system: The experiment uses cross-polarized twin beams generated via parametric down-conversion in a periodically-poled KTiOPO4 (PP-KTP) waveguide operating in the telecommunication wavelength range.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the resource-saving analysis tools using single-click probability. It then details the measurement of normalized factorial moments up to $m=n+1$ to test the violation of classical light conditions, culminating in quantitative results for multi-photon state characterization.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, providing robust experimental techniques to verify the non-classical nature of light sources, which is foundational for quantum communication and computation.
